### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A32 appeared in fewer traces and less often per trace: participation fell from about 60 in 100 cases to about 48 in 100 cases, and mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.14 to about 0.79, a drop of roughly 0.35 [OCC001].
- Repetition of A32 also became less common: among traces containing it, about 31 in 100 showed it more than once in the earlier window, versus about 21 in 100 in the later window [OCC001].
- The difference is large relative to random re-splits of the pooled data: about 995 in 1000 reference comparisons showed a smaller difference, and the profile rests on 119 traces before and 95 after [OCC001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one control-flow item qualified across 50 tested units, where roughly 0.25 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process — a count an unchanged process typically produces — so the apparent decline of A32 could be a sampling fluctuation despite its high empirical strength [OCC001].

- Trace participation: 0.595 → 0.475 (difference -0.12)
- Recurrence support: 0.31 → 0.21 (difference -0.10)
- Observed change: 0.35
- Empirical strength: 0.995 (about 99.5% of reference comparisons had smaller differences)
- Support: before 119 traces (out of 200), after 95 traces (out of 200)

No time items (TWAIT), no resource items (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources. Wait — the screening has a "time" family, but the evidence items themselves contain no TWAIT items. The instruction says "Only if the evidence contains time items (TWAIT)". The evidence list contains only OCC001, which is CF_OCC. So no time discussion, no resource discussion.

Now the judgement:

Screening comparison: control_flow family has 1 item with 0.25 expected without change. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

Here: 1 item vs 0.25 expected. One item when fewer than one is expected — this is exactly the example given. So the count is of the same order as the expectation. Therefore: Insufficient evidence.

Even though the single item looks strong (empirical strength 0.995, meaning the difference is unusual for random splits), the screening comparison says one item when 0.25 is expected is what an unchanged process typically produces. So the answer is "Insufficient evidence".

Also, the time family: 0 items, 0.007 expected — nothing there.

So:

### Observed differences

Describe: Activity A32 occurred less often in the later window. Mean occurrences per trace dropped from about 1.14 to about 0.79 (a decrease of 0.35 occurrences per trace). Trace participation fell from about 60 in 100 cases to about 48 in 100 cases. Recurrence support (share of traces with the activity where it repeats) fell from about 31% to about 21%. The difference is unusual for random re-splits (empirical strength about 99.5 out of 100 reference comparisons had smaller differences). Support: 119 traces before, 95 after — reasonably substantial samples, but still one item.

No other differences; no time or resource items.
